claims.text: WTaTiVZr has enhanced plastic strain relative to pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
WTaTiVZr has enhanced fracture toughness relative to pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
Severe lattice distortion and nanoscale grain-boundary solute segregation primarily govern the proposed enhancement in plastic strain and fracture toughness.
Severe lattice distortion and grain-boundary solute segregation together increase dislocation pinning.
Severe lattice distortion and grain-boundary solute segregation alter the fracture mechanism under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr creates heterogeneous internal stress fields.
The heterogeneous internal stress fields promote nanoscale solute segregation or nanoprecipitate formation at grain boundaries.
Grain-boundary segregation or nanoprecipitates enhance dislocation pinning.
Pure tungsten fractures predominantly by a transgranular mode under the specified conditions.
WTaTiVZr shifts fracture from the predominantly transgranular mode attributed to pure tungsten toward a mixed or intergranular mode.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit a higher dislocation-pinning density than pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr will show nanoscale segregation or precipitate formation at grain boundaries.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater plastic strain than pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater fracture toughness than pure tungsten.
The proposed mechanism applies in a temperature range where diffusion-mediated nanostructural evolution occurs without destabilizing the high-entropy matrix.
Outside that temperature range, additional variables may dominate the mechanical response.

contradictions.description: The alloy is predicted to have improved fracture toughness while shifting toward more intergranular fracture, but no explanation is provided for how the proposed intergranular contribution produces rather than undermines the toughness improvement.

The hypothesis specifically attributes enhanced plastic strain and toughness to lattice distortion and grain-boundary segregation, but the falsification rule requires dislocation structures, boundary chemistry, and fracture modes all to be indistinguishable. A failure to improve plastic strain or toughness despite observing the proposed mediators would therefore not satisfy the stated falsification rule.
